@@ -0,0 +1,109 @@
+---
+name: repro-first
+description: Demonstrate a reported CamCraft bug through MCP or a pinning test on current main before fixing it. Preserve the before reading for the PR, and stop with issue evidence when the bug does not reproduce or reproduction is unsupported.
+---
+
+# repro-first - measure the bug before changing its cause
+
+Use this skill before a bug fix, including a takeover or review fix.
+Read [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md), [gh-issues](../gh-issues/SKILL.md),
+[work-issue](../work-issue/SKILL.md) and the
+[ownership guard](../issue-claims/references/ownership.md).
+AGENTS.md takes precedence. Reproduction is not permission to change an
+unclaimed issue or a branch that another writer or reviewer owns.
+
+## 1. Establish the baseline
+
+1. Read the full issue and comments. Identify the input, steps, expected
+   result and observed result. Search for an existing fix or duplicate PR.
+   Check the claim, ownership, effort and release-cut prerequisites in
+   `work-issue` before edits. Record the current process rules.
+2. Fetch the canonical repository's latest `main`. Record its full SHA.
+   In a fork, follow [fork-sync](../fork-sync/SKILL.md): this check does not
+   merge upstream `main` into the fork's `main` or refresh an existing PR.
+   Use an isolated worktree at the recorded upstream commit if necessary.
+   Never switch or pull a checkout that is running a gate.
+3. Keep the implementation unchanged while collecting the before reading.
+   Record the operating system, build command, binary provenance and
+   relevant feature flags. Do not use an old binary as evidence for the
+   fetched `main`. Keep user data private; prefer a small original fixture.
+4. For a takeover, also record the PR's exact starting head. A failure only
+   on that branch is not a reproduced bug on current `main`. Report the
+   distinction; do not refresh the branch merely to obtain a baseline.
+
+## 2. Reproduce before writing the fix
+
+Choose the smallest supported route:
+
+- **MCP:** load [camcraft-mcp](../camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md). Use the shipped
+  tools to create or open the minimal document and run the reported steps.
+  Save the requests, actual responses, diagnostic or numeric reading, and
+  expected result. The binary must come from the recorded baseline.
+  A server connection or screenshot alone does not demonstrate the bug.
+- **Pinning test:** add a focused assertion in an existing domain directory
+  suite, in the lowest crate that provides its imports. Load
+  [gate](../gate/SKILL.md). Run the named test against the unchanged baseline
+  implementation and save its actual failure. The failure must assert the
+  reported behaviour, not a build error, missing fixture or service outage.
+
+Do not start the implementation fix until one route demonstrates the bug.
+For either route, record the input and exact command so another contributor
+can repeat it. Use only permitted clean-room inputs. Do not run generated
+G-code on machinery as part of this software procedure.
+
+### Outcomes that are not a reproduced bug
+
+| Observation | Action |
+|---|---|
+| Current `main` gives the expected result | Stop the fix. Post the SHA, input, command, expected result and actual reading on the issue. Ask for the missing case through that evidence; do not invent a failure or close the issue. |
+| The build fails, MCP lacks the required operation, or the fixture is unavailable | State that reproduction is unsupported or blocked, not that the bug is absent. Post the limitation and partial evidence on the issue. Stop until a supported test or input is available. |
+| The issue changes prose only | Demonstrate the missing or incorrect text and run focused documentation checks. Mark runtime reproduction not applicable. Do not claim that MCP or a regression test failed. |
+| A known-fail test already records the defect | Run that exact test and confirm the expected assertion fails on the baseline. An ignored test that was never run is not evidence. |
+
+A new test committed red on purpose must use AGENTS.md's **Tests that start
+red use the known-fail marker**, not plain `#[ignore]`. Keep the open issue,
+full test name, target and expected panic prefix accurate. A temporary red
+run for a fix does not justify shipping an unmarked failing test.
+
+## 3. Fix, then repeat the same measurement
+
+1. Continue `work-issue` only after the baseline demonstrates the defect.
+   Preserve the input and assertion. Do not weaken the expected result to
+   make the test pass, suppress a diagnostic, or remove a safety refusal.
+2. Make the smallest fix. Run the same MCP sequence or named test again.
+   Record the after reading and exact fixed head. For an MCP reproduction,
+   add a pinning test where possible; state any remaining coverage limit.
+3. Confirm that the test detects the defect: its recorded baseline run
+   must fail at the relevant assertion and its fixed run must pass.
+   If the assertion changed, repeat the baseline check in an isolated
+   worktree. Do not overwrite unrelated work to manufacture a red run.
+4. Run the selected quick gate and the other applicable checks from `gate`.
+   A dry run or zero-step plan is not a test pass. Keep full heavy lanes,
+   snapshots and release gates in their required lanes. Report unrelated
+   failures separately; do not replace actual output with expected output.
+
+## 4. Put the before reading in the PR
+
+Use this structure with actual readings, not placeholder success text:
+
+```text
+Reproduction before fix:
+- Baseline: <canonical main full SHA; build/binary provenance>
+- Input and environment: <fixture path and relevant settings>
+- Command or MCP requests: <repeatable sequence>
+- Expected: <assertion, diagnostic or numeric result>
+- Observed before: <actual result; log or evidence link>
+- Pinning test: <full name and baseline assertion failure, or limitation>
+
+After fix:
+- Head: <full fixed SHA>
+- Same measurement: <actual result; evidence link>
+- Checks: <commands and actual results>
+- Not exercised: <limits, unsupported routes or unrelated failures>
+```
+
+For prose-only work, replace the runtime fields with the before text,
+location and focused checks. Keep the normal PR fields from `work-issue`,
+including `Process change: yes` when applicable. Publish as a draft first.
+Verify publication and release writer ownership before independent review.
+A contributor pre-check is not a counted collaborator review.

+---
+name: takeover
+description: Continue another author's stalled CamCraft PR only with recorded approval or a stale claim. Check claims, branch ownership, maintainer edits, refresh timing and exact heads; preserve commits and provide a patch if a push is refused.
+---
+
+# takeover - continue a PR without competing with its author
+
+Use this skill for one named PR, not a sweep of old PRs. Read
+[AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md), [gh-issues](../gh-issues/SKILL.md),
+[issue-claims](../issue-claims/SKILL.md) and the
+[ownership guard](../issue-claims/references/ownership.md) first.
+AGENTS.md takes precedence. This procedure grants no repository permissions.
+
+## 1. Establish whether a takeover is allowed
+
+1. Read the complete issue and PR threads, reviews, labels and commits.
+   Search for other PRs with the same head repository and branch.
+   Record the issue, PR, head repository, branch, base and full exact SHAs.
+2. Stop during a release cut (an open `release/*` PR). Do not take a `P?`,
+   `blocked` or `needs-research` issue for implementation.
+3. Require the author's explicit approval in the thread, or evidence that
+   the claim is stale under **A claim must be live**. Link that evidence.
+   The age of the PR, silence on the PR, or a missing label is not enough.
+4. A contributor's claim remains live if any of these is true:
+   - The claimant has an open PR for the issue, even an old draft.
+   - The claimant's branch has a commit in the last 48 hours.
+   - The claimant commented on the issue in the last 48 hours.
+   Only when all three are absent can it be stale. Owner-account agent
+   claims use the separate 4-hour rule in `issue-claims`.
+5. Do not push while the author is active. Approval alone does not release
+   an active writer or reviewer. Obtain an explicit handoff and release.
+   A released writer record does not release a live issue claim. If the
+   claimant changes, record the old claim's withdrawal or release, then a
+   new claim. An ended claim never revives without a new claim line.
+6. Follow the ownership guard before dispatch or local work. A live writer
+   or counted reviewer means stand down and name the owner and record URL.
+   A counted reviewer has no expiry timer. Two active records mean STOP
+   until one owner releases. Failed or incomplete reads also mean STOP.
+
+## 2. Record one writer and prepare the existing branch
+
+1. Use `work-issue`'s existing-PR path. Keep the issue and its branch;
+   do not create a competing fix or overwrite the author's history.
+   Post or confirm one writer record on the upstream issue, and link it
+   from the PR. Include the approval or stale-claim evidence.
+2. Read the record back by its comment URL. Re-read the complete threads
+   and the exact remote head. Confirm the sole named writer before edits.
+3. Fetch the author's exact head into a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/`.
+   Check that it equals the recorded `Starting head` and `Expected remote`.
+   Preserve the author's commits. Never rebase or force-push, including
+   `--force-with-lease`. Do not switch or edit the main checkout.
+4. Check GitHub's `maintainer_can_modify` field for the PR. Maintainer edits
+   let a base-repository maintainer update a permitted fork branch; the
+   flag does not give an arbitrary contributor push access. Confirm the
+   actual account, head repository and exact branch. Never infer access
+   from the flag alone. Do not use the author's credentials.
+5. Preserve the draft rules. New PRs open as drafts. An orange `conflicts`
+   verdict requires the `resolve-conflicts` draft-before-push procedure,
+   including its SAME exception. Ordinary review fixes keep a ready PR
+   ready under **A review finding does not make a PR a draft again**.
+   A takeover does not authorize an extra draft/ready cycle.
+
+## 3. Make and check the bounded change
+
+- Use [work-issue](../work-issue/SKILL.md) for the fix and its pinning tests.
+  For a bug, load [repro-first](../repro-first/SKILL.md) before the fix.
+- A takeover is not permission to refresh a branch. **Refresh only at merge
+  time** still applies: the author's agents handle **Own blocked PRs
+  first**, the PR is next in the merge batch, or the author chooses a
+  refresh while pushing a review fix. Otherwise leave the base alone.
+- For an allowed refresh, use
+  [resolve-conflicts](../resolve-conflicts/SKILL.md). Merge, never rebase.
+  Stop if both sides change the same logic or a safety rule can be lost.
+  Compile affected code with `cargo check --tests -p <affected-package>`,
+  one package at a time, including incoming base changes and shared inputs.
+  A prose-only refresh gets focused documentation checks, not a code pass.
+- Run the applicable checks on the final committed tree. Record the exact
+  head, commands, results and exclusions. A zero-step quick plan is not
+  proof that documentation or code passed tests.
+
+## 4. Publish once, or provide the patch
+
+1. Immediately before a push, repeat the ownership guard's pre-push reads.
+   Re-read the claims, writer/reviewer records, PR head and remote branch.
+   Do not build or edit between those reads and the push. A moved head
+   means STOP; preserve the local commits and report both exact SHAs.
+2. With confirmed maintainer-edit permission and a completed handoff, push
+   plainly to the recorded author's branch, not to upstream `main`.
+   A rejected push means STOP. Do not retry with another credential,
+   rebase, reset, branch deletion or force-push.
+3. If GitHub refuses the push, preserve the worktree and local commits.
+   Make a repository-relevant patch with
+   `git format-patch --stdout <starting-head>..HEAD`.
+   Post it in a PR comment as a fenced patch, or attach the patch and link
+   it from that comment if it exceeds the comment limit. Check that it
+   contains only the intended commits and no private data. Do not silently
+   open a replacement PR or push to a different branch.
+4. Write one result comment that names the starting head, each added
+   commit, the reason for each change, checks and any refusal. For a patch,
+   include its application base and state that the remote did not change.
+   For a successful push, verify remote and PR heads against local HEAD;
+   record `Published head` and `Expected remote` against the writer URL.
+5. Release writer ownership with its record URL, final exact head and the
+   published result or stopped reason. Read back the comment and patch.
+   Keep the issue open until its fix merges. Hand off for independent
+   review; never count your own pre-check as a collaborator review.
+
+## Completion check
+
+- Approval or all required stale-claim evidence is linked.
+- The author is not writing; the old claim and owners have valid releases.
+- One writer, the exact remote head and refresh permission were checked.
+- Original commits remain; no force-push or competing branch was used.
+- The result comment traces commits, reasons, checks and any refused push.
+- Remote publication or the patch was read back; ownership was released.

+## #3913 - Contributor takeover and reproduction procedures
+
+**Decided:** Add original `takeover` and `repro-first` skills and two routing
+rows in `AGENTS.md`. Reuse the existing claim, ownership, fix, gate and
+conflict procedures rather than defining another ownership mechanism.
+
+**Why:** A stalled PR needs an explicit handoff, not an age-based push.
+An open PR keeps a contributor claim live. A bug fix needs an actual before
+reading on current `main`, not a successful connection or an assumed failure.
+The procedures record refused pushes and unsupported reproduction honestly.
+
+**Considered and dropped:** Do not copy the SolidCraft skills. Their ideas
+are prior art; CamCraft's current rules supply the procedure. Do not add a
+new timeout, a replacement-PR automation, a runtime framework or CAM changes.
+Do not change `PROCESS_VERSION`; the merging session owns the bump.
+
+**Cost to change later:** Edit these two skills and their routing rows.
+Keep references consistent with `issue-claims`, its ownership guard,
+`work-issue`, `resolve-conflicts` and `fork-sync` when those rules change.
